text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Iran sent fighter plane squardron to Syria.
- Israeli interior minister intends to consult with Prime Minister Netanyahu before approving construction of Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem.
- EU summit to discuss proposal to demand Israel lift closure of West Bank and Gaza and open Gaza port.
- Bezeq workers to strike over plan to open telecommunications market to competition.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu adds National Infrastructure Minister Sharon to ministerial team negotiating peace.
- Israel rejects Egyptian mediation bid with PLO.
- Netanyahu's settler brother-in-law says prime minister and family pressing him to leave Hebron.
- France's Danone to pay $56 million for 20 percent of Strauss Dairies.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Foreign Minister Levy reiterates: There will be no peace with Syria without compromise on the Golan.
- Heavy pressure on coalition members to support budget cuts.
GLOBES
- Israeli telecommunications market to be opened to competion by the end of 1998.
- November trade gap, $526 million, lowest in past 15 months.
- Provident fund withdrawals dropped in November to 382 million shekels compared with 1.06 billino shekels in October.
JERUSALEM POST
- Head of parliament's finance committee says panel won't okay child allowance cuts.
- Netanyahu rejects Egypt's foreign minister as Hebron mediator.
- Jewish neighbourhood approved for Ras al-Amud.
- Palestinians try to stop farm work in disputed Jordan Valley land.
- Israel Discount Bank forecasts 2.5 percent to three percent GDP rise in 1997.
- Trade deficit shrinking since May.
